note: Three synthetic defects, one per outcome, so a test can prove that the QA severity ladder, the UAT crosswalk and the release-readiness known-issues rule reach the same blocking outcome for each of them. F03 of the 2026-09-23 360 audit: the QA ladder and the UAT table used to disagree about S1 and S2, so the same defect blocked or shipped depending on which document was open.

defects.story: Submitting an expense report fails silently once the report contains a foreign-currency receipt, and there is no other way to submit it.
The report can be submitted, but only by exporting it to CSV and re-uploading it, because the in-app submit step drops the receipt attachments.
The Submit button label renders one size smaller than the rest of the form.

gap_class_note: A known-issues row may leave the severity ladder only by naming which readiness gap it is, and its Issue cell must show that gap in its own words. The bare marker `not a defect` was an unguarded escape hatch: a real product defect could be relabelled with nothing failing. The words below are the evidence a row must carry for the class it claims.
